full_judgment:
7. The learned Subordinate Judge has written a clumsy judgment. It seems that he has dismissed the suit on three grounds. One is that the plaintiff has failed to prove, his case to the hilt. Other is that the suit is not maintainable. The third one is that the suit is barred by limitation. The learned Subordinate Judge asked himself as to what kind of suit it is. Is it a suit for money or a suit for declaration? Then he answered that it is not understandable as to what kind of suit it is. 

 17. The learned Advocate for the respondent submits that the suit is barred by limitation. According to the learned Advocate the cause of action of this suit arose on 29.9.73 when admittedly it was found that the cases in question were lying in broken condition and that the period of limitation for this suit is three years either under Article 48 or 49, First Schedule, Limitation Act as it is a case of injuring or wrongfully detaining the goods by the Bank according to the plaintiff's allegations. 

 Period of limitation. 

 19. Column 1 and 3 of Articles 48 and 49 must be read together and as a whole and then the purposes thereof will be clearly understood. Wrongs contemplated in both the Articles have the same meaning as they have in the law of torts and as such the relationship between the plaintiffs and the defendants in the suits falling under these Articles must be that of strangers, devoid of any contractual obligations, the former being the wronged and the latter being the wrong-doer. Therefore, submissions of the learned Advocate must be rejected. We hold that Article 120 is applicable in the instant suit wherein the period of limitation is six years from the date when the right to sue accrued. 

 21. We have already stated that by its letter, ext. 10, dated 14.2.74 though the defendant admitted the pilferage of the imported goods in question, but informed the plaintiff that it would not allow the plaintiff to take part deliver), thereof "until final settlement of the LIM dues". But the defendant remained silent even after receiving the plaintiff's proposal in the letter Ext. 16, dated 21.6.82. The defendant for the first time denied the in the written statement filed in the suit. Therefore the date of cause of action in this suit is not the essence of the suit and filing of the written statement denying the plaintiff's claim is to be accepted as a cause of action of this suit. This suit is not barred by limitation.
